messages:
alex: heads up — infra-ci is racking up failures on the gke nodepool creation step in the terraform apply matrix. multiple jobs stuck for 20+ minutes. anyone else seeing this?

maya: yup, saw 3 failures in the matrix. logs show API quota errors during nodepool create in us-west1, then a terraform apply hang waiting on operations.

samir: same. plus some runs fail earlier with cache-restore 403 from s3 which causes a job restart and then we hit the GKE quota window. feels like a cascade.

alex: here's a snippet from the failing apply:
```
Error: googleapi: Error 403: Quota 'COMPUTE_REGION_INTERNAL_NODEPOOLS' exceeded for project 12345 in region us-west1, quota limit: 10
  on modules/gke/nodepool.tf line 42, in resource "google_container_node_pool" 
```

jordan: Oof. That quota is per-region. We've had bursty canaries + gpu-canary jobs creating ephemeral nodepools. When the matrix parallelism (8x) kicks in it piles up.

maya: note also the GH Action runner preemptions earlier today — a lot of ephemeral runners got reclaimed, so some runs retried and replayed the nodepool creation quickly. runner churn + cache failures = bad combo.

devops-bot: build 1982345678-6 failed: terraform apply timed out waiting for node pool creation. See: https://ci.internal/redwood/builds/1982345678-6/logs

samir: temporary mitigation idea: reduce matrix parallelism for infra repos to 3, and switch the nodepool creation to use resource-level locking so only one job provisions at a time. GH Actions has concurrency/resource_group we can use.

alex: agreed. also we should delay GPU canary runs to a separate schedule to avoid contending with PR CI. open to suggestions for quick change?

maya: for quick patch I can add "concurrency: \n  group: infra-ci-provision\n  cancel-in-progress: true" to the apply job and change matrix.include to limit concurrent creates. also add a small random sleep before create to reduce thundering herd.

jordan: longer term we need to stop creating nodepools in PR CI. Options: pre-provision a shared test nodepool with labels and taints, or use a mock provider for lightweight tests. Also quota alerts in pagerduty are missing for region-specific limits — we should surface that.

samir: agreed on alerts. I'll raise a ticket to add per-region quota dashboards and an automated fallback that switches to a lower-capacity node template.

alex: one more wrinkle — the cache restore 403s are coming from an old boto credential rotation that messed up the deploy key for our cache bucket. that's why some runs retry mid-provision. CC @security to follow up.

maya: in the short term I pushed a patch to the infra-ci workflow in branch ci/serial-nodepool-provision (PR up). it reduces matrix concurrency and adds the resource_group lock for the create step. will monitor.

devops-bot: PR ci/serial-nodepool-provision opened by maya (#4123).

alex: perfect. let's monitor for the next 6 hours and if we still see quota spikes we'll implement the pre-provisioned shared nodepool approach. thanks all :thumbsup:

jordan: FYI if anyone needs to rerun a stuck job, do not just re-run all matrix jobs — cancel and re-run the failed job once the quota window clears. replays while throttled just waste quotas.

samir: filed infra ticket INF-1028 (add region quota dashboards + pod to auto-detect high churn) and assigned to eng-infra. linking notes here: https://tickets.internal.redwood/INF-1028

maya: monitoring looks cleaner after the patch, only 1 retry so far. will keep an eye and post updates.

alex: thanks — closing this thread for now unless anything else crops up.
